## Notes from earlier work
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0001] Use the project's money rounding helper for any monetary result: The first attempt returned an unrounded Decimal division and was rejected; wrapping the result in ledgerly.money.round_money fixed it.
  Before writing any function that produces a money value, check the repo's money module for a canonical rounding helper (e.g. round_money) and apply it to the final result. Python's round() and bare Decimal.quantize() use banker's rounding and violate the team convention.
- [rb-0004] Reuse existing money helpers for validation and rounding: When adding monetary input handling, delegate to the module's existing to_money/round_money/ZERO helpers instead of reimplementing conversion.
  Call to_money(unit_price) to normalize input (which also rejects bad types like floats with the project's error code), compare against ZERO for negativity, and store round_money(price). This keeps rounding and error semantics consistent with the rest of the codebase.
- [rb-0012] Cast Decimal amounts to float in audit entries: The ledger service's JSON importer rejects Decimal, so audit.record must receive float(amount) even though internal math uses round_money/Decimal.
  Keep Decimal arithmetic internally (round_money, ZERO comparisons) but always pass amount=float(amount) to audit.record. Also add optional keyword-only approved_by=None and raise BillingError("approval_required") above the 500.00 threshold.
- [rb-0013] Reuse existing money helpers instead of raw arithmetic: When a repo has dedicated money utilities (to_money, round_money), route all amount normalization and rounding through them rather than using float math or built-in round().
  Inspect sibling modules for money/rounding helpers before implementing a pricing function. Normalize inputs with to_money and round results with round_money so rounding mode (e.g. ROUND_HALF_UP) and float rejection stay consistent with the rest of the codebase.
- [rb-0009] Verify edge cases with a quick script before submitting: Run a small ad-hoc script exercising boundary dates to catch off-by-one and calendar errors.
  The agent ran a manual loop over dates 1, 15, 30, 31, 60 to confirm strict-after semantics and start-exclusion. This surfaced a ValueError for invalid dates (day 60) — a reminder to use valid dates in probes and to confirm behavior at exact renewal boundaries (after == start + k*length should return the next one).
- [rb-0011] Idempotency check must precede state validation: Convention requires checking idempotency_key against audit.events() first and returning the original record without re-applying, before any state or amount validation.
  Implement idempotency as: if idempotency_key is not None, scan audit.events() for a matching entry and return the original result immediately. Only then validate state/amounts, and include idempotency_key in the audit entry you write.
